    Extracting Hom-orthogonal pairs of equal class #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.exists_residual_pair_of_noniso {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] {X Y : FGModuleCat R} (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : f ≠ 0) (hni : ¬CategoryTheory.IsIso f) :
    ∃ (Q : FGModuleCat R) (K : FGModuleCat R) (q : X ⟶ Q) (j : K ⟶ Y), CategoryTheory.Epi q ∧ CategoryTheory.Mono j ∧ GrothendieckGroup.of Q - GrothendieckGroup.of K = GrothendieckGroup.of X - GrothendieckGroup.of Y ∧ (¬CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero Q ∨ ¬CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero K) ∧ FGModuleCat.moduleLength Q < FGModuleCat.moduleLength X ∧ FGModuleCat.moduleLength K < FGModuleCat.moduleLength Y

    Cancelling a nonzero noninvertible map across a class relation removes the same image class from each side. The residual terms cannot both vanish.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.exists_orthogonal_pair_of_not_equalClassHom {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] (h : ¬EqualClassHom (FGModuleCat R)) :
    ∃ (X : FGModuleCat R) (Y : FGModuleCat R), GrothendieckGroup.of X = GrothendieckGroup.of Y ∧ GrothendieckGroup.of X ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ (f : X ⟶ Y), f = 0) ∧ ∀ (f : Y ⟶ X), f = 0

    A failure of the equal-class Hom condition yields a nonzero equal-class pair for which Hom vanishes in both directions.

    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.exists_quotient_split_of_not_epi {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] {A B : FGModuleCat R} (f : A ⟶ B) (hf : f ≠ 0) (hne : ¬CategoryTheory.Epi f) :
    ∃ (L : FGModuleCat R) (Q : FGModuleCat R) (p : A ⟶ L) (q : B ⟶ Q), CategoryTheory.Epi p ∧ CategoryTheory.Epi q ∧ GrothendieckGroup.of B = GrothendieckGroup.of L + GrothendieckGroup.of Q ∧ FGModuleCat.moduleLength L ^ 2 + FGModuleCat.moduleLength Q ^ 2 < FGModuleCat.moduleLength B ^ 2

    A nonzero nonepimorphism splits the target class into two quotient classes of strictly smaller total squared length.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.exists_subobject_split_of_epi {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] {A B : FGModuleCat R} (f : A ⟶ B) [CategoryTheory.Epi f] (hf : f ≠ 0) (hne : ¬CategoryTheory.IsIso f) :
    ∃ (L : FGModuleCat R) (Q : FGModuleCat R) (i : L ⟶ A) (j : Q ⟶ B), CategoryTheory.Mono i ∧ CategoryTheory.Mono j ∧ GrothendieckGroup.of A = GrothendieckGroup.of L + GrothendieckGroup.of Q ∧ FGModuleCat.moduleLength L ^ 2 + FGModuleCat.moduleLength Q ^ 2 < FGModuleCat.moduleLength A ^ 2

    A noninvertible epimorphism splits the source class into two subobject classes of strictly smaller total squared length.
